text:
Elaine: Quick sync — what's our current leaning for the internal control-plane APIs? proto-first gRPC with an HTTP gateway, or REST-first? cc @Samir @Kevin :thinking:
Samir: proto-first. typed contracts, smaller payloads, faster service-to-service. codegen wins for multi-language stubs.
Kevin: I get typed contracts, but browser clients and some infra teams want JSON. adding a gateway for external traffic feels inevitable and adds ops surface.
Anya: telemetry/console team note — dashboards and traces assume HTTP semantics (status codes, JSON bodies). gRPC needs extra mapping to keep UI simple.
Samir: we can keep internal traffic gRPC and run a managed HTTP gateway only for external endpoints. runtime routing policy: prefer grpc for low-latency internal paths, fallback to gateway when needed.
Kevin: gateway as a translation layer worries me — single point for versioning bugs. we've had proto->JSON drift in past mappings.
Samir: agreed, which is why the canonical contract should be the proto. gateway is a thin translation layer generated from the proto. automation for tests should catch mapping mismatches.
Elaine: quotas/ACLs question — easier at the gateway (edge) or closer to service (sidecar)? what about tenant-scoped routing and cost accounting?
Samir: quota enforcement can live at edge or envoy sidecar. If internal -> grpc, attach tenant headers in an auth filter and enforce at the edge OR at the per-cluster quota service. both are feasible.
Anya: console UX: we need a consistent telemetry spec. propose mapping gRPC status -> HTTP codes and standardized metadata fields (tenant_id, route, model_id). Without that, dashboards will fragment.
Kevin: dev DX: curl + JSON is trivial for quick tests. Can we provide a local dev shim that exposes HTTP/JSON generated from the proto for dev usage only?
Samir: yes. dev-shim that compiles protos to a tiny HTTP facade + mocks. production: envoy gateway or our managed gateway. streamlining that gives us both DX and perf.
Kevin: streaming use-cases: logs, KV cache invalidation, real-time slot availability — gRPC streaming is much cleaner than chunked JSON.
Anya: agree — long-lived streams and pub/sub style flows should be gRPC-only. console will read aggregated metrics over HTTP.
Elaine: rough policy then: canonical proto + gRPC for internal service-to-service and streaming; generated HTTP gateway for external/public endpoints; dev-shim for local JSON; telemetry mapping spec and quota placement RFCs.
Samir: example proto snippet for reference:
```proto
syntax = "proto3";
package redwood.control;
message RouteRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  string path = 2;
}
service Router {
  rpc Route(RouteRequest) returns (RouteResponse);
}
```
Kevin: +1 to that approach. also: we need e2e tests that run the gateway translation during CI to catch drift.
Anya: I'll draft the telemetry mapping doc with concrete fields and example dashboards (error rate, tail latency split by transport).
Elaine: action items: Samir - write proto-first RFC with gateway + dev-shim ops appendix; Kevin - prototype local HTTP shim + CI gateway translation test; Anya - telemetry mapping doc; I'll coordinate infra for quota placement and rollout UX.
deploy-bot: Reminder: canary rollout scheduled 2026-03-22 09:00 UTC for gateway v2. :bell:
Kevin: noted. also we should decide SLAs for gateway translation latency (p95 budget).
Samir: propose p95 < 10ms for simple passthrough routes, higher for heavy transcoding. include perf budgets in RFC.
Anya: one more: how do we surface transport in the console? show transport (gRPC/http) per-route and allow filter on it. helps debugging.
Elaine: good idea. I'll add console filter request to the action list. If no objections I'll put the RFC and the three docs in next Monday's sync. :thumbsup:
Samir: +1
Kevin: +1
Anya: +1
